# Employment Contract Templates — Full Documentation Overview

## Skill Purpose

This skill provides templates and patterns for creating **legally sound employment documentation**, including employment contracts, offer letters, employee handbooks, and HR policies.

> ⚠️ **Important Disclaimer:** These templates are for **informational purposes only** and **do not constitute legal advice**. Always consult with qualified legal counsel before using any employment documents.

---

## When to Use This Skill

- Drafting employment contracts
- Creating offer letters
- Writing employee handbooks
- Developing HR policies
- Standardizing employment documentation
- Onboarding documentation

---

## Core Concepts

### 1. Employment Document Types

| Document | Purpose | When Used |
|----------|---------|-----------|
| **Offer Letter** | Initial job offer | Pre-hire |
| **Employment Contract** | Formal agreement | Hire |
| **Employee Handbook** | Policies & procedures | Onboarding |
| **NDA** | Confidentiality | Before access |
| **Non-Compete** | Competition restriction | Hire/Exit |

### 2. Key Legal Considerations

```
Employment Relationship:
├── At-Will vs. Contract
├── Employee vs. Contractor
├── Full-Time vs. Part-Time
├── Exempt vs. Non-Exempt
└── Jurisdiction-Specific Requirements
```

---

## Available Templates

### Template 1: Offer Letter
Contains sections for:
- Position details (title, department, reports to, location, start date, employment type)
- Compensation (base salary, bonus, equity)
- Benefits (health insurance, 401(k), PTO, holidays)
- Contingencies (background check, right-to-work verification, required signed documents)
- **At-Will Employment** statement
- Acceptance block with signature lines

### Template 2: Employment Agreement (Contract Position)
Contains 9 numbered sections:
1. **Employment** — position, duties, best efforts, location
2. **Term** — either at-will or fixed-term language
3. **Compensation** — base salary, bonus, equity, benefits, expenses
4. **Confidentiality** — definition, non-disclosure, return of materials, survival
5. **Intellectual Property** — work product, assignment, assistance, prior inventions (Exhibit A)
6. **Non-Competition & Non-Solicitation** — customers and employees (with jurisdiction enforceability note)
7. **Termination** — for cause, without cause, by employee, severance, effect of termination
8. **General Provisions** — entire agreement, amendments, governing law, dispute resolution, severability, notices, assignment, waiver
9. **Acknowledgments** — execution block for both parties plus Exhibit A

### Template 3: Employee Handbook Policy Section
Contains policy sections for:
- Equal Employment Opportunity
- Anti-Harassment (prohibited conduct, reporting procedure, investigation)
- Work Hours and Attendance
- Paid Time Off (with accrual table by years of service)
- Sick Leave
- Holidays
- Code of Conduct
- Technology and Communication (acceptable use, monitoring, security)
- Social Media Policy
- Acknowledgment form

---

## Best Practices

### Do's
- **Consult legal counsel** — Employment law varies by jurisdiction
- **Keep copies signed** — Document all agreements
- **Update regularly** — Laws and policies change
- **Be clear and specific** — Avoid ambiguity
- **Train managers** — On policies and procedures

### Don'ts
- **Don't use generic templates** — Customize for your jurisdiction
- **Don't make promises** — That could create implied contracts
- **Don't discriminate** — In language or application
- **Don't forget at-will language** — Where applicable
- **Don't skip review** — Have legal counsel review all documents

---

## Reference Resources

- [SHRM Employment Templates](https://www.shrm.org/)
- [Department of Labor](https://www.dol.gov/)
- [EEOC Guidance](https://www.eeoc.gov/)
- State-specific labor departments

---

# Example: Offer Letter for a Senior Software Engineer

Below is the Offer Letter template (Template 1) applied to a senior software engineering position. Placeholders to customize are shown in `[BRACKETS]`:

```markdown
# EMPLOYMENT OFFER LETTER

[Company Letterhead]

Date: [DATE]

[Candidate Name]
[Address]
[City, State ZIP]

Dear [Candidate Name],

We are pleased to extend an offer of employment for the position of Senior
Software Engineer at [COMPANY NAME]. We believe your skills and experience
will be valuable additions to our team.

## Position Details

**Title:** Senior Software Engineer
**Department:** Engineering
**Reports To:** [VP of Engineering / Engineering Manager Name]
**Location:** [Office Location / Remote / Hybrid]
**Start Date:** [Proposed Start Date]
**Employment Type:** Full-Time, Exempt

## Compensation

**Base Salary:** $[AMOUNT] per year, paid [bi-weekly/semi-monthly/monthly] in
accordance with the Company's standard payroll practices, subject to applicable
withholdings.

**Bonus:** Eligible for an annual discretionary bonus of up to [X]% of base
salary, based on company and individual performance. Bonus payments require
active employment at the time of payment.

**Equity:** [X shares/options of common stock vesting over 4 years with a
1-year cliff, subject to the terms of a separate Stock Option Agreement /
Not applicable]

## Benefits

You will be eligible for our standard benefits package, including:
- Health insurance (medical, dental, vision) effective [date]
- 401(k) with [X]% company match
- [X] days paid time off per year
- [X] paid holidays
- [Remote work stipend / Professional development budget / Other benefits]

Full details will be provided during onboarding.

## Contingencies

This offer is contingent upon:
- Successful completion of background check
- Verification of your right to work in [Country]
- Execution of required employment documents including:
  - Confidentiality Agreement
  - [Non-Compete Agreement, if applicable and permitted in your jurisdiction]
  - Employee Innovation and IP Assignment Agreement (covering work products,
    inventions, and software code created during employment)

## At-Will Employment

Please note that employment with [Company Name] is at-will. This means that
either you or the Company may terminate the employment relationship at any
time, with or without cause or notice. This offer letter does not constitute
a contract of employment for any specific period.

## Acceptance

To accept this offer, please sign below and return by [DEADLINE DATE — typically
5-10 business days]. This offer will expire if not accepted by that date.

We are excited about the possibility of you joining our engineering team. If
you have any questions, please contact [HR Contact] at [email/phone].

Sincerely,

_________________________
[Hiring Manager Name]
[Title / CTO or VP of Engineering]
[Company Name]

---

## ACCEPTANCE

I accept this offer of employment and agree to the terms stated above.

Signature: _________________________

Printed Name: _________________________

Date: _________________________

Anticipated Start Date: _________________________
```

---

## Key Customization Notes for Engineering Roles

When adapting this template for a software engineer, pay special attention to:

1. **IP Assignment Is Critical** — Ensure the IP assignment agreement is explicitly referenced as a contingency. Software engineers create intellectual property daily, so the Company must own all code, designs, and inventions.

2. **Equity Details** — Engineering offers frequently include equity. If included, reference the separate Stock Option Agreement and confirm terms like vesting schedule, cliff, and exercise price are covered there.

3. **Remote/On-site Language** — Specify location clearly and address any travel or occasional on-site requirements, since many engineering roles are remote or hybrid.

4. **Exempt Status** — Software engineers are typically classified as **Exempt** under the FLSA — confirm this designation fits the role's duties and the salary threshold for your jurisdiction.

5. **Non-Compete Caution** — Non-competes for engineers are **restricted or unenforceable in some jurisdictions** (e.g., California). Verify enforceability with local counsel before including one.

6. **Background Checks** — For security-sensitive engineering work, you may also add a note about additional screening (e.g., credit check, reference verification, or background check for government contracts).

Remember: **customize every field in brackets, verify jurisdiction-specific requirements, and have legal counsel review the final document before sending.**
